t: You're looking at the Florence Nightingale Faculty of Nursing and Midwifery, part of King's College London. It carries the name of the founder of modern nursing, who established the school on the ninth of July, 1860. It is described as the world's first nursing school to be continuously connected to a fully serving hospital and medical school. For the rest of the nineteenth century it was a model for training schools across the UK and the Commonwealth. Nightingale came to prominence in the Crimean War, where she organised care for wounded soldiers and cut death rates by improving hygiene.
